members.name: AssetsRoot
members.doc: Asset root the collector resolves project-relative references against.

members.name: Scenes
members.doc: Comma-separated scene paths. ScenesFile wins when both are set.

members.name: ScenesFile
members.doc: One scene path per line.

members.name: RedirectsPath
members.doc:
--redirects: the project's Config/Redirects.ini, so a scene that still names
a renamed asset path or field cooks what it means.

members.name: OutPath
members.doc: Where the pack list goes; empty logs it instead.

members.name: CookTexturesDir
members.doc:
Intermediate directories for the cooked .mtex / .mmodel sidecars; empty
packs the sources raw.

members.name: StrictRefs
members.doc:
A reference the collector cannot resolve fails the cook instead of
shipping a package that is missing what the game asks for.

members.name: CookAll
members.doc:
--cook-all: every texture and model source under AssetsRoot is listed
(and so transcoded), not only what a scene reaches. A texture a Visual Script
graph, code or a soft path loads, or a project with no scene in the cook
at all, used to ship its PNG/FBX raw — full RGBA8 in VRAM, no LODs, no
meshlets. Scenes become optional.

members.name: FromCommandLine
members.doc:
--assets --scenes --scenes-file --registry --out --cook-textures
--cook-meshes --strict-refs --cook-all, as `mbt cook` and `mbt package`
pass them.

types.name: FCookDeps
types.doc:
The selective-cook dependency walk: every asset the shipped scenes reach,
laid out globals-first then per streaming sector, written as the file list
MeafBuilder packs. Pure CPU, so packaging runs it with no GPU and before any
engine init.

members.name: Run
members.doc:
Returns a process exit code of its own: `mbt package` cooks with the
release binary, which carries no test harness, so a --strict-refs
failure has to be the process's own verdict or it would report success
on exactly the build that must not ship broken.

types.name: FGameLaunchSettings
types.doc:
What a game host needs from the project manifest before the engine exists:
the product name that owns the per-user data root, the window it opens and
the Steam relaunch identity.

members.name: SplashImage
members.doc:
Project Settings › Game Window › Game Splash (player.splashImage):
relative to the project root, empty for none — the default, so a game
opens straight onto its first frame as an Unreal game does.

types.name: FGameHostBootstrap
types.doc:
The packaged-run bootstrap every host of the player shares — MowoGame,
and RuntimeTests when it drives the player against a staged package. One copy,
so what the tests prove about a package is what the shipped exe does.

members.name: ApplyBuildInfoManifest
members.doc:
Reads BuildInfo.json from the game root, the working directory or the
executable dir: crash attribution, the per-product data root, the build
id, the crash reporter and analytics. A manifest (or an unwritable game
root) marks the run as packaged. True when it named the product.

members.name: ApplyProjectCrashReportClient
members.doc:
An unpackaged run of a game: the project's Config/Engine.ini
[CrashReportClient] section (else the legacy .mproject crashReporter.dsn)
becomes the crash settings every report carries. A BuildInfo.json read by
ApplyBuildInfoManifest wins. True when the project configured anything.

members.name: ArmModuleSignatureGate
members.doc:
With the game's signing key registered (FMeafKeyRing), every module the
player loads by name — engine feature modules, plugins, game modules —
must carry a signature from that key, and the working directory and PATH
leave the DLL search. Call after the keys and before Engine::Initialize,
which loads the first of them. True when the gate armed.

members.name: FindProjectFile
members.doc:
--project, else Game.mproject (or the first *.mproject) in the game
root, the working directory, then the executable dir. Empty when none.

members.name: HasProject
members.doc:
True when there is a project to start: the manifest on disk, or the one a
package carries inside its engine pak.

members.name: ReadLaunchSettings
members.doc:
The manifest on disk when there is one, else the copy cooked into the
content archive.

members.name: ReadSplashImage
members.signature: static std::string ReadSplashImage(const std::string& projectPath, const FGameLaunchSettings& settings)
members.doc:
The Game Splash's encoded bytes (PNG, JPEG or BMP): the file beside the
project in a dev run, else the GameSplash.<ext> `mbt package` put in the
engine pak. Empty when the project has none.

members.name: ApplyProductName
members.signature: static void ApplyProductName(const FGameLaunchSettings& settings, bool buildInfoProductSet)
members.doc:
The game's product name owns its per-user data root — call before
Engine::Initialize picks the log directory. BuildInfo.json wins when it
already named a product.

types.name: MGameEngine
types.doc:
The standalone game player's engine — UE5's UGameEngine analog.
No Layer/LayerStack: main() Initializes, calls StartGame(), Run()s.

members.name: StartGame
members.doc:
Load project + start scene, enter play mode. Call after
Engine::Initialize, before Run(). Returns false when the project
or start scene cannot be loaded.

members.name: StopGame
members.doc:
Stop play mode and release game resources. Call after Run()
returns, before Engine::Shutdown.

members.name: GatherPsoCache
members.doc:
Author tool behind `MowoGame --gather-pso`: after StartGame, loads
every material the project registers, starts every graph pipeline
variant each one can ask for, and merges the session's pipeline records
into the committed Config/PsoCache.mdfb the package ships. Coverage then
follows the content instead of whatever a recording session happened to
play past. Returns the process exit code.

members.name: BeginStartupPresentation
members.doc:
The start a player sees, as an Unreal game does it: no engine splash.
The (hidden) window shows the moment the graphics device exists, with a
black frame — or the project's Game Splash image, fitted — and every
startup stage after that pumps the OS queue and presents again, so a
long level load or pipeline compile never reads as "not responding".
Call before Initialize and route the init-progress callback to
PumpStartupFrame. `origin` is the process start the "[Startup]" log
lines measure from. The window keeps the last startup frame until the
first game frame replaces it.

members.name: RequestTravel
members.signature: void RequestTravel(const std::string& scenePath, const FTravelOptions& options = FTravelOptions())

members.name: PushUIScreen
members.signature: int32_t PushUIScreen(const std::string& assetPath, int32_t zOrder = 1000, bool modal = false)
members.doc:
Game-code surface for the ArcUI screen stack: push/pop code-driven
screens (pause, main menu, loading) and set the input mode. Modes map
to InputManager's EInputMode; UIOnly and GameAndUI show the cursor,
GameOnly leaves cursor policy to game code. A modal pushed screen
forces UIOnly until it pops.

members.name: ReconcileModalInputMode
members.doc:
Apply "a modal screen forces UIOnly" from the stack's own answer.
Called every tick, so every push path is covered.

members.name: RegisterUIAction
members.signature: void RegisterUIAction(const std::string& action, std::function<void()> handler)
members.doc:
Named UI action handlers the .ui event sink dispatches to. A Visual Script
sink later registers the same way — action string in, callable out.

members.name: HasFatalError
members.doc:
True when StartGame failed (e.g. project not found) and the engine
showed the error box instead of exiting silently.

members.name: EnterErrorMode
members.doc:
Native "project not found" message box + Stop(). Call after the window
is up but the project failed. Virtual because a host with nobody in
front of it must not block on a modal box until its watchdog fires.
